verdict.rationale: Obsidian stores notes as local plain-text Markdown files, so an agent can read and write them directly on disk. Obsidian also documents a headless Sync client that works without the desktop app and is described as useful for agents and automated workflows. However, nothing in the evidence shows a documented local API, vendor API, or MCP server. Obsidian URI and the plugin Vault API both run inside the app, so headless access depends on raw file manipulation rather than a structured interface. Missing for 10: a documented local/vendor REST API or official MCP server for note read/write, and independent hands-on corroboration of agent workflows.
